narrative:
That 1–5 scoreline against Oranje is a result that exposes every flaw in my pre-match reasoning, and I'm not going to dress it up. I correctly identified that Sweden's wing-backs leave dangerous transition corridors behind them — but I pointed that finger at Japan and effectively waved it away when it came to Oranje, who have Brobbey and Gakpo operating at a level that punished those exact spaces four times over. I predicted a Sweden win on the premise that Gyökeres and Isak would be the decisive quality gap, and they weren't — Elanga's consolation aside, Blågult were second to everything, and the Dutch front line was simply at a different level than anything I priced into my 0.47 win probability. The one thing I got technically right was identifying transition vulnerability as a structural concern — I just assigned it to the wrong fixture entirely, and in doing so, failed to weight Oranje's attacking threat with anything close to the gravity it deserved.
